Subject: Post-call recap + data request: token cadence, budget range, batching assumptions

Hi Samira — great to speak today. Quick recap and a few asks so we can size a realistic POC and give you an accurate $/1M token target. TL;DR: please share a sample hourly token distribution for a typical week and a ballpark monthly budget range.

Key items from today's discovery:
- Workloads: mix of short chat queries (~40% of calls, 15-40 tokens) and document summarization (~60% of calls, 1k-5k tokens).
- Target latency: conversational paths expect ~150ms p95 for short queries; summary paths can tolerate 500–1,000ms.
- Volume profile: anticipated starting run-rate ~120M tokens/month with seasonal peaks up to ~350M.
- Must-haves: data isolation for PHI, audit logs, and deployment in us-west.

Asks / next steps from NeuroHealth so we can size correctly:
1) Sample traffic (hourly or 15-min granularity) for one week (attach CSV if possible).
2) A target budget band (example: $10k–$30k/month) or target $/1M tokens you're comfortable with.
3) Priority endpoints — which feature(s) (chat vs summarization) must be highest SLO?

Tentative POC approach we propose: dedicated trial instance with continuous batching enabled for chat endpoints, and configurable concurrency for summarization workers. We attached a short economic-assumptions template you can fill to speed things up.

Attachments: economic-assumptions-template.xlsx (template)

I'll follow up with Marissa and Grace to propose a technical deep-dive once we have the sample token cadence.

Best,
Rishi

- The 120M/mo is conservative; Q4 marketing push could push sustained traffic to ~220–300M/mo.

Hi Samira — appreciate the sample and the budget range, that's very helpful. High-level estimates and notes below (ballpark until we validate against the exact token mix in the CSV):

Ballpark unit economics (dedicated trial config, us-west):
- Continuous batching enabled for chat endpoint, conservative batch-window: 20–40ms aggregation.
- Expected effective $/1M tokens (steady-state):
  * Light batch density (low concurrency, few short messages): ~$850–$1,200 / 1M tokens
  * Moderate batching (typical for steady 120–250M/mo): ~$550–$900 / 1M tokens
  * High-density batching (sustained >300M/mo, high request consolidation): ~$350–$600 / 1M tokens

Notes:
- These ranges assume model choice in our Redwood catalog with quantization-friendly variants and standard KV caching. Summarization workloads (long sequences) add token-expense but often lower per-token cost when amortized across longer outputs.
- To meet chat p95 targets (~150–200ms), we recommend: concurrency cap for chat workers (per-GPU) and a short batch-max-window so short queries don't wait longer than ~40ms for batch formation. Continuous batching reduces unit cost by ~20–45% relative to one-request-per-invocation, depending on traffic consolidation.

Answers to your questions:
1) We can deliver a preliminary $/1M estimate within 48 hours after we parse the CSV and a short mapping of which columns represent user-visible tokens vs internal processing tokens. The ballparks above are a starting point.
2) Concurrency caps affect batch density: higher concurrency increases the opportunity for large batches (lower $/token) but risks increased queuing tail for individual requests if the batch window is long. We typically tune: small batch window (20–50ms) + per-endpoint concurrency limit to balance p95 latency with cost.

Suggested next steps:
- Rishi: propose 2 time slots for a technical deep-dive this week (30–45m) where Grace (infra) can map instance sizing and batching knobs.
- Samira: confirm which columns in the attached CSV map to request vs response tokens and share any retention/compliance constraints.

I'll also draft a quick POC configuration that maps your budget band to a 30-day dedicated trial with clear success metrics (p95, cost/1M).

Cheers,
Marissa
